answer: The network defeats sybils using synchronized, uncacheable pointer-chasing challenges across RAM. An isolated bare-metal agent traverses its address space with a marble-smooth latency profile. Conversely, sybils multiplexed on shared hypervisors trigger bus contention, smearing read times into an erratic dune of tail stalls. Hiding this hardware overlap behind a sable cloak of proxy relays fails because added network hops breach the deadline. Attackers must provision dedicated physical memory channels for each identity, making mass creation scale at hardware cost.
